definition: Leabra stands for local, error-driven and associative, biologically realistic algorithm.
details: It is a model of learning which is a balance between Hebbian and error-driven learning with other network-derived characteristics. This model is used to mathematically predict outcomes based on inputs and previous learning influences. Leabra is heavily influenced by and contributes to neural network designs and models, including emergent.

explainer.lead: Leabra is a biologically realistic learning algorithm balancing Hebbian and error-driven learning. It is used to model learning mathematically and has influenced neural network designs.

tiers.eli5: Like a student who learns partly by repetition and partly by correcting mistakes, roughly the way a brain might.
tiers.practitioner: Researchers use it to build models that predict outcomes from inputs and prior learning; a pitfall is that biological realism brings complexity that general-purpose deep learning frameworks do not assume.
tiers.paperLevel: Leabra stands for local, error-driven and associative, biologically realistic algorithm; it combines Hebbian and error-driven learning with other network-derived characteristics.

explainer.example: A Leabra network is trained on input patterns and uses its prior learning influences to predict outcomes for new inputs.
